title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a space X (probably in a tame or semi-analytic sense) and 'figures' in X. A figure is a decomposition of a closed part |F| of X into connected strata U_i, whose closures X_i are the closed cells. An 'elementary figure' (figure élémentaire) is a figure that is the closure of a single top stratum, with its induced stratification. Σ'_F is the set of elementary sub-figures of F, i.e. the closed cells X_i with their induced figure structures.

Page 6 proved two conditions equivalent for figures F, F': (a) a condition on closed cells, X_i ∩ X'_j being saturated, which forces X_i = X'_j; and (b) any two strata U_i of F and U'_j of F' are either disjoint or equal. The proof is by induction on sup(dim F, dim F').

Page 7:
(1) F and F' are called compatible when these conditions hold.
(2) Compatibility is tested on elementary pieces: F and F' are compatible iff every F_0 ∈ Σ'_F is compatible with every F'_0 ∈ Σ'_{F'}. The 'only if' holds because the strata of an elementary sub-figure are strata of the ambient figure. The 'if' holds because every stratum lies in its closed cell, which is an elementary sub-figure.
(3) This lets one work purely combinatorially. Let F_él be the set of elementary figures of X, ordered by the sub-figure relation ≤. On it, put the reflexive symmetric relation R ⊂ F_él × F_él, 'F_0 compatible with F'_0'. Equivalently, take the set S ⊂ P_2(F_él) of compatible 2-element subsets. This makes F_él a poset carrying a compatibility graph.
(4) NB: if F_0 ≤ F'_0 they are compatible. More generally, two elementary sub-figures of a common figure F are compatible, since all their strata are strata of F.
(5) Definition: a configuration is a set of pairwise compatible figures, i.e. a clique of the compatibility graph. A configuration of dimension n is a clique of n-dimensional figures.

Page 8 completes the picture. A figure F corresponds to Φ = Σ'_F ⊂ F_él, which is (a) downward closed, (b) a configuration, and (c) locally finite. Conversely, every such Φ comes from exactly one figure.

So figures in X are identified with locally finite, downward-closed cliques in the poset of elementary figures with its compatibility relation. This is a 'face-poset' or 'polyhedral complex' style description of stratified spaces, taken globally over all possible cells of X at once.
errors: Index slip in the NB. It reads 'si F'_0, F''_0 ≤ F, donc F_0 et F'_0 sont compatibles'; the conclusion should name the same two figures as the hypothesis, i.e. 'F'_0 and F''_0', or the hypothesis should read 'F_0, F'_0 ≤ F'.

The equivalence 'compatible iff all elementary sub-figures are pairwise compatible' tacitly assumes that the induced structure on a closed cell X_i consists exactly of strata of F. This holds for frontier-condition stratifications but is not stated here.
'Configuration of dimension n: set of n-dimensional figures' presumably means elementary figures, i.e. closed n-cells. As written, it is ambiguous whether the figures must be elementary.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two stratified figures: strata pairwise disjoint or equal, equivalently a condition on closed cells; testable on elementary (single closed cell) pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Compatible / common-refinement-free stratifications; polyhedral complexes whose faces intersect in common faces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical polyhedral topology (complexes in PL topology); Ziegler-style polyhedral complex axioms
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches tame topology and dévissages but not this formalism, as far as I know

ideas.what: Encoding the totality of possible figures in X by the poset F_él of elementary figures plus a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, as a graph R ⊂ F_él×F_él or a set S ⊂ P_2(F_él).
ideas.modern_name: Face-poset / abstract cell complex encoding; poset with coherence (compatibility) relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (face posets of regular CW complexes, 1984); Girard (coherence spaces, 1987) for the abstract structure

ideas.what: Configurations as pairwise compatible sets (cliques). With page 8: figures correspond bijectively to downward-closed, locally finite configurations.
ideas.modern_name: Configurations of a prime event structure (down-closed, conflict-free sets); cliques of a coherence space; clique/flag complexes

missed.claim: Take incompatibility as the conflict relation. Conflict is inherited upward: if F_0 is incompatible with F'_0 and F'_0 ≤ F''_0, then F_0 is incompatible with F''_0. So the triple (F_él, ≤, incompatibility) satisfies the axioms of a prime event structure in the sense of Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel. Grothendieck's figures are then exactly its configurations (down-closed, conflict-free, here locally finite). He even uses the same word 'configuration'. Forgetting the order, (F_él, compatibility) is a coherence space in Girard's sense, and figures are certain cliques.
missed.quote: on introduit une relation (symétrique, réflexive) R ⊂ F_él × F_él ... Configuration : Ens. de figures deux à deux compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests treating the 'space of all stratifications/cell structures' of a tame space as the domain of configurations of an event structure. This would give order-theoretic or domain-theoretic tools, such as refinements and directed sups of figures, for tame-topology and moduli-of-stratification questions. It also offers a geometric source of event structures. I know of no literature linking tame stratifications to event structures or coherence spaces.

missed.claim: The global combinatorial object, the poset of all elementary figures of X with its compatibility graph, is introduced as the basic data of an analysis situs. Its own topology or homotopy type (e.g. the clique/order complex) and its functoriality in X are not developed on this page.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to modern work on spaces of triangulations and stratifications and on exit-path categories. It is a possible combinatorial foundation for Grothendieck's 'tame topology' programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The content itself is close to standard polyhedral/face-poset reasoning. The notable point is the abstraction: the poset of all possible cells, a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, and figures as down-closed locally finite 'configurations'. This coincides strikingly with event structures and coherence spaces, which arose independently in computer science around the same time. That is an unrecorded structural parallel, but not a deep new result.
transcription_corrections: 'relation symétrique, réflexive)' is likely '(relation symétrique, réflexive)', i.e. a parenthetical with the opening parenthesis missing.

In the NB, the image reads 'Mieux, si F'_0, F''_0 ≤ F' with conclusion 'donc F_0 et F'_0 sont compatibles entre elles'. This is an index slip by the author, not a transcription error, but it should be flagged.
On the next page, 'Fil' should probably be read as 'F_él' (ensemble des figures élémentaires), consistent with this page.
